newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IMF seen confident in Hong Kong through handover.
newsitem.headline: IMF seen confident in Hong Kong through handover.

text.p: Hong Kong's promotion to the category of advanced economy showed the International Monetary Fund's confidence in the territory ahead of its handover to China, an IMF official said on Monday.
Graham Hacche, chief of the IMF's World Economic Studies Division, said Hong Kong was reclassified in the organisation's World Economic Outlook released in April for three reasons.
Hacche told reporters that Hong Kong's per capita income levels were now as high or higher than members of the old industrialised countries category.

Hong Kong also had a diversified economy that did not rely on any particular activity, and the territory not only had a well developed financial sector but was a major international financial centre, he said.
Advanced economies was a new category since the old concept of industrialised nations was no longer sufficient, Hacche said.
Along with Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan, Korea and Israel joined the industrialised nations in the new category, he said.
According to the IMF report, Hong Kong's gross domestic product is expected to grow 5.0 percent in both 1997 and 1998, compared to 4.8 percent in 1995 and 4.5 percent in 1996.
The territory reverts to China at midnight of June 30 after more than 150 years as a British colony.
